notes: No sub-theme marked separate: 'flowers named after people' (magnolia, dahlia) are themselves words named after people, and every names sub-theme (girls', boys', gems, months, places, colors, trees...) gives words that read as first names. Within 'names that are places' and 'names that are colors' a few members read more as the place or colour than a name (Tennessee, Everest, Kenya, Asia, Magenta, Tawny, Azure); they carry familiarity 3-5 but could be dropped. No fiction found to remove (Zelda kept as a real old-fashioned name; kaiju kept as a generic genre word). No digit members fit these themes. Names: Turkish, Irish and Latin American names now use their native letters and accents (Ayşe, Barış, Siobhán, Seán, José, María); Irem kept without the Turkish dotted capital; Japanese, Russian, Chinese and Indian names stay in plain romanisation. Yiddish schmuck, putz, dreck keep adult=1.
